4b75b1321a.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow Above 5,000 feet. Additional snow accumulations 3
to 8 inches above 5,000 feet; 1 to 3 feet above 7,000 feet. Winds
gusting as high as 50 mph along the Sierra Crest.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
4b75b1321a.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

88a8e9c6f1.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in freezing fog.

* WHERE...Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.
88a8e9c6f1.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

2c673f2095.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Additional snow accumulations of 3 to 6 inches
mainly above 7000 feet. Winds gusting as high as 40 to 50 mph.

* WHERE...Spring Mountains-Red Rock Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel will be difficult in higher elevations. Blowing
snow could significantly reduce visibility. Strong winds could
cause damage to trees and power lines.
2c673f2095.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

4644fa69d7.description:
* CHANGES...Snow amounts reflect remaining accumulations.

* WHAT...Heavy snow. Snow accumulations up to 4 inches. Wind gusts of
20 to 30 mph, with ridgetop wind gusts as high as 70 mph.

* WHERE...Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Thursday evening and Friday
morning commutes.
4644fa69d7.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.
Check with Caltrans for the latest road conditions.

48c8c62746.description:
* CHANGES...Snow amounts reflect remaining accumulations. Wind gusts
were updated.

* WHAT...Heavy snow. Snow accumulations up to 4 inches for
communities around Lake Tahoe with up to 6 inches above 7000 feet.
Wind gusts of 30 mph for Truckee and Lake Tahoe communities, with
ridgetop gusts as high as 70 mph.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Thursday evening and Friday
morning commutes. Strong winds could cause damage to trees and
power lines. Strong winds and rough waves on Lake Tahoe will create
hazardous conditions for small watercraft.
48c8c62746.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.
Check with Caltrans and NDOT for the latest road conditions.

13575b9749.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow above 4000 feet. Additional snow accumulations of
8 to 12 inches above 4000 feet, with up to 18 inches over highest
peaks. A dusting to a few inches are possible as low as 3500 feet.
Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 4000 feet, including Highway 50,
Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108, Southern Cascades
above 4000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the evening commutes. Gusty winds
could bring down tree branches and significant reductions in
visibilities.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels around 4000-5500 feet, lowering
briefly down to around 3500 feet early Friday morning. Heaviest
snow is expected through the afternoon hours, with snowfall rates
1-2+ inches per hour.
13575b9749.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.
